job.title: Finance & Accounts Specialist - Driving Miss Daisy
job.description:
We love building this team; this is a great opportunity to join a commercially successful, community-facing, New Zealand wide business. If you are experienced in accounts processing and are known for your attention to detail and forensic ability to pick up anomalies, then this could be a great role to consider.  

Driving Miss Daisy is recognised as the nationwide market leader in the companion driving sector - they are loved by many for their service and support across the country. Their highly effective franchise model operates in 85 different franchise territories from Invercargill to Kerikeri, with their head office based here in Havelock North. They have recently secured a significant contract with ACC and they want to expand their team to ensure they continue to meet their goal of administrative excellence. Their continued aspirations for the development and growth of their franchisees means that they rely increasingly on accurate data and quality analysis to help drive commercial performance for every franchise owner across the country. 

Working closely with the Senior Data Analyst and reporting to the General Manager, your focus will be on the administration that sits around ACC invoicing across each of the franchises. This will include remittance reconciliation, processing franchisee-specific payment batches, franchisee compliance and reporting, as well as supporting with general accounts administration.

There is an exciting new system integration here, and ample scope to make this role your own. Competency with Excel and Xero will be crucial, and you must have the ability to read beyond the numbers and uncover anomalies and errors across sets of data. This role will see you engaging directly with ACC to query and resolve any issues. Importantly, you will bring a well-developed, inquisitive communication style, where you are not afraid to question how things are done.

If you have the required expertise and are keen to join a business that makes a significant difference empowering the lives of kiwis every day, then we would love to hear from you. Please apply directly through this portal, or for further information, call the team at Populous People for a confidential chat on 06 875 8446.

job.title: Sales Director - Nibblish
job.description:
If you are an expert in leading and expanding FMCG sales channels and categories this could be a great sales leadership opportunity. You will be driving both the New Zealand and Australian sales strategy for Nibblish, and you get to do it from the home base of Hawkes Bay. Career and great living all in one.
  
Nibblish is a fast-growing ANZ snacking brand, with its head office in the heart of Havelock North. Join a great team and an exciting brand; delivering innovative fruit products into more than 2,000 mainstream supermarkets across New Zealand and Australia. The business is achieving strong double-digit growth, led by Australia, where its presence with Coles and Woolworths continues to expand. Your role is to protect, expand and grow its shelf presence even further.
  
As Sales Director, reporting directly to the CEO and founder, you will own and evolve the ANZ commercial delivery for Nibblish. Your role will be to build on the strong growth already established with Coles, Woolworths AU, Foodstuffs NZ and Woolworths NZ. And you will have genuine scope to define the next horizon of sales growth and execution across Australia and New Zealand. 
  
Sales and relationship management, and commercial leadership intersect here. You will be responsible for delivering the ANZ sales and operating margin budgets, and will work closely with the CFO to support profitability analysis. You will be someone who can actively bring forward profitable growth initiatives; identifying new customers, new channels, optimising promotional plans, and adjacent category opportunities will sit with you.
  
This role sits across the end-to-end commercial relationship with every major existing retailer Nibblish trades with in Australia and New Zealand. Familiarity and experience in dealing with Coles and Woolworths AU will be highly regarded.  And strong account and category management relationships in Foodstuffs NZ and Woolworths NZ will be essential. You will represent Nibblish directly with these retailers, negotiating trade terms, establishing joint business plans, and ensuring optimised portfolio ranging. And you will also work closely with distributor partners, as well as build direct relationships with key independent and specialty retailers.
  
This is suited to an experienced FMCG sales leader and senior account manager. If you are not already at sales director level, this move will feel like your next natural step. Either way you will know that channel presence and shelf space is everything in FMCG. You must have the category management expertise and the resilience to build strong relationships with key decision makers and influencers in store and in market across New Zealand and Australia.
  
Join a great crew, passionate about their work. You will be well rewarded and supported by business owners determined to ensure balance and enjoyment in your day. If you have the FMCG sales leadership expertise, and you relate well to the pace and innovation of SMEs on a growth trajectory then please apply through this portal or telephone Rachel Cornwall at Populous People on 0272 565620 to learn more.

job.title: Embedded Systems Design Engineer
job.description:
This is an exciting time to be joining a world leading wildlife tracking sales and engineering team. You will be based from Hawkes Bay New Zealand, whilst working closely with the Canadian based parent company.

The core essence of this highly specialized role is all about writing the code for the micro-controllers that make hardware come alive. And in this very clever business it is hardware that enables wildlife of all shapes and sizes to be tracked.  Our client specialises in manufacturing devices capable of tracking creatures spanning avian, freshwater, marine and terrestrial wildlife. This career opportunity places you at the heart of their technology offering.

This company’s Radio, Acoustic, Archival, GPS and Satellite instruments deployed on animals throughout the world provide insight to animal behaviour, how and where they spend their lives. We need an embedded systems design engineer to design, implement, and verify new products and feature, as well as to support existing product designs.

To be successful in this role you will need hands-on embedded systems design experience. You will be a good systems programmer and you’ll have solid knowledge of general circuit theory. Other key experience we are looking for includes:
  • Bachelor level qualification at the minimum, with hands-on software/firmware design experience,
  • Software exposure to the likes of C, C#, Java or similar,
  • Excellent familiarity with test & measurement equipment normally used in design work,
  • Good dexterity with miniature circuits and components;
  • Excellent communication skills (written and oral) and demonstrated ability of documenting the engineering work, very good command of English language is a must;
  • Practical knowledge of firmware design principles
  • Up-to-date familiarity with the latest electronic components, primary and secondary batteries, sensors and signal conditioning would be welcome assets as well.
  • Experience with programming techniques for ultra low-power battery operated systems would be a great asset although can be taught on the job.
This is a great role for a practically minded systems design engineer. If this sounds like you, then we really want to hear from you. Please apply through this seek portal or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Workplace Relations Specialist
job.description:
We are looking for an experienced workplace relations specialist with strong employee and industrial relations experience, sound employment law knowledge, a pragmatic approach, and exceptional relationship-building skills.  This is a great opportunity to join a highly regarded organisation in a specialist role supporting leaders and the People team to navigate complex employment matters with confidence, fairness and sound judgement.

Employing a large and diverse workforce, this organisation is committed to creating positive outcomes for its people, customers and communities.  With a strong values-based culture and a genuine focus on its people, it offers a collaborative environment where expertise is valued and meaningful contribution is encouraged.

In this newly established role, you will provide specialist ER and IR expertise across the organisation, working closely with People Partners, leaders and the wider People team. A key part of the role will be leading and supporting complex or higher-risk employment matters, including disciplinary and performance processes, grievances, investigations, workplace conflict, organisational change and employment disputes.  You will provide specialist industrial relations advice, support the interpretation and application of collective agreements, employment agreements and legislative obligations, and contribute to constructive union engagement and consultation.  Importantly, this role is about more than managing individual employment matters.  You will also help strengthen organisational ER/IR capability by developing practical frameworks, guidance and tools, identifying emerging or systemic employment risks, and coaching leaders and People colleagues to support fair, consistent and sustainable practice.

To be successful, you will bring deep and proven experience across both ER and IR ideally gained within a complex environment.  You will enjoy guiding people through challenging situations and be known for your ability to operate with diplomacy, discretion, sound judgement and a people-centered approach.  A relevant tertiary qualification is expected, while additional study or expertise in employment law will be highly regarded.  If you have the required expertise and this opportunity aligns with your next career move, we would love to hear from you. Please apply through this portal or contact Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Communications and Engagement Manager - Water Hawke's Bay
job.description:
This new opportunity will have you steering and guiding the communications and engagement for the new regional water services entity across the Hawke’s Bay region. This role is crucial in ensuring Water Hawke’s Bay (WHB) is ready to begin delivering drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater services from 1 July 2027, with a focus on providing safe and reliable water services for generations to come.

As Engagement and Communications Manager, you will be steering Water Hawke’s Bays’ communications and engagement strategy. This enduring programme of work is centred around building trust with communities, mana whenua, workforce and regulators, while standing up the channels, brand and systems the organisation will run on day one. You will ensure provision of structured, consistent communications to governance bodies and shareholder councils, and provide strategic and operational leadership across communications, engagement, customer experience, and reputation management.

You'll work with key leaders across the entity to support the refinement of the organisation’s purpose, vision, values, and identity. And you will ensure the organisation’s narrative, stakeholder relationships, customer experience foundations, and public communications are coherent, trusted, and aligned with the aspirations of Hawke’s Bay communities.

To be successful you will need senior leadership experience in managing strategic communications in politically complex environments. The ability to engage with and present to key regional leaders and stakeholders including mana whenua will be essential. Relatability to utilities and infrastructure, and experience operating in multi shareholder environments will be highly regarded. Your brand and organisational identity development expertise and experience creating messaging that engages across different audiences and channels. will ensure you have real impact here. A creative and collaborative mindset, balanced with a strong focus on delivery and results is essential in this environment. Experience in steering teams and leading leaders through transformation change and high impact projects will be highly regarded.

This is an exciting and impactful role. If you have the required strategic communication expertise and want to be a part of something very special, we would love to hear from you. Please apply through this portal. Or call Rachel Cornwall at Populous People on 0272 565620 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Production Engineer - Lotek
job.description:
We are looking for a talented hands-on electronics engineer to join our client’s very special business. This is an exciting time to be joining this world leading wildlife tracking sales, engineering, and manufacturing team. Based local, impacting global. You will be working from their Hawke’s Bay operation, whilst working closely with the Canadian parent company. It’s a great place to work; a really friendly crew, and a well-funded business on a continuous and sustained growth path.
  
This will be perfect for those with five plus years experience and relevant electronics, mechatronics or electrical engineering qualifications. It may also be really well suited to a seasoned engineer wanting a fresh new challenge.
  
This is a very clever business - the technology you will be working with enables researchers across the globe to track wildlife of all shapes and sizes.  Our client specialises in manufacturing devices capable of tracking avian, freshwater, marine and terrestrial species. Their Radio, Acoustic, Archival, GPS and Satellite instruments deployed on animals throughout the world provide insight to animal behaviour, and how and where they spend their lives.
  
This is a proactive, solutions focused role. You will be a pivotal link, providing technical support to R&D engineers, the production team, customers, and sales. Your days will be comprised of a range of hands-on electronic engineering tasks, fault finding, testing and prototyping, developing and writing production documentation, streamlining and improving manufacturing processes. A soldering iron will feel as comfortable in your hand as a ball point pen.
  
To be successful here, you must be competent in electronic circuit design and testing, production processes, handling bills of materials, work instructions, and fault and root cause analysis. There is a great deal of communication required in this role. You will be a key figure in building relationships between the local and global members of Lotek family and must have excellent command of the English language (written and spoken).

Check out www.lotek.com This is a great way to balance your career development with the chance to work on a global technology offering, all the while living in sunny Hawke’s Bay. If your electronics engineering expertise aligns and you are keen to be part of this smart bunch, please apply through this seek portal, or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 to learn more.

job.title: Mechanical Design Engineer - Lotek
job.description:
This is an exciting time to join a world-leading wildlife tracking engineering, manufacturing and sales team. You will be based in Hawkes Bay New Zealand, whilst working closely with the Canadian parent company.
  
This is a very clever business - the hardware and material you will be working on enables wildlife of all shapes and sizes to be tracked across the globe.  Lotek specialises in manufacturing devices that track creatures spanning avian, freshwater, marine and terrestrial wildlife forever aiming to innovate with smaller, stronger lighter devices. Their Radio, Acoustic, Archival, GPS and Satellite instruments deployed on animals throughout the world provide insight to animal behaviour, and how and where they spend their lives.
  
This career opportunity places you at the heart of their technology offering.
  
The core of this role is to design and create prototypes, moving prototypes into manufacturing, and enhancing existing product design and offerings. You will work closely with the engineering, production, and product management teams to design and bring to market new products and to refine existing products. You will ensure their smooth transition to commercial production as well as refining and redeveloping existing devices. Throughout this process, you will create and maintain documentation for all new parts, components, and assemblies. You will provide technical direction and guidance to technical staff and assist with training and development initiatives. A continuous improvement mindset with a focus on higher quality and efficiency is essential.
  
This role is suited to a tertiary-qualified engineer, with a track record ideally in packaging design, prototyping and verification testing. You must be able to demonstrate experience in design and hands-on fabrication of light production jigs and fixtures. Ideally you will have expertise relating to small battery-powered electronic packaging including mouldings. Either way, you must understand and show competence in the behaviour of epoxies, fabrics, glues, silicones and 4-axis CNC machining.  Proficiency with SolidWorks is important and knowledge and expertise in materials a definite plus.
  
You would be a self-starter with the ability to show initiative and think outside the box. Our products are highly unique and often fall outside conventional industry norms, incorporating materials sourced from a wide range of applications.
  
If you have the expertise to step into this very special role then we would love to hear from you. This will allow you to balance your career development and the chance to work on a global technology offering whilst living in sunny Hawkes Bay where great schooling and great lifestyle is just a given.
Please apply through this Seek portal or phone the team at Populous for a confidential discussion to learn more. Telephone 06 875 8446.

job.title: People and Culture Manager
job.description:
Great businesses are built by great people, and this newly created HR leadership role presents a unique opportunity to help shape the next chapter of Lattey Group’s people journey.  There is a strong platform here – you will be a key appointment, with a clear focus on influencing and further enhancing culture, growing organisational capability, and partnering closely with leadership to support long-term success.  For someone seeking a role with genuine and meaningful impact, this is an opportunity worth exploring.

Lattey Group, with a 100 plus strong team, is a proudly New Zealand-owned infrastructure business with deep roots in Hawke's Bay and Levin, and a reputation built over generations. From civil construction and precast concrete manufacturing through to crane hire and specialist infrastructure solutions, their people play a critical role in delivering projects that help connect communities and support growth across New Zealand.

Reporting directly to the recently appointed CEO, you will be shaping the HR function from the ground up and partnering closely with all teams across the business as they enter a new chapter of growth and enhancement.   Your scope includes fostering a high-performing culture, strengthening leadership and team and organisational capability, and ensuring the people structures and systems are in place for Lattey Group’s continued growth and success.  You’ll be across the full employee lifecycle; providing trusted guidance to the CEO and wider business teams on organisational and leadership development, recruitment, performance, ER, engagement and wellbeing.  This is a role for someone who thrives on variety, enjoys balancing strategy with hands-on delivery, and wants to build capability while creating people practices that are practical, fit-for-purpose, and aligned to business objectives. You will have the opportunity to influence decision-making at the highest level while also remaining connected to day-to-day operations and the people who make the business successful. 

This is suited to a nimble, forward facing and savvy HR leaders that hold a relevant tertiary qualification and are technically sound in senior HR and people leadership practices.  You have an approach that is authentic, contemporary, and empathetic and a passion for collaboration and driving a culture of learning, continuous improvement, and service delivery.  You may currently be in a similar HR leadership role, or you are possibly looking for your next growth step to the executive level.  Relatability to construction and manufacturing based workforces will be highly regarded, although not essential. Either way, Lattey Group will be a great place for the right person to really have a hugely positive people impact for the future.  If this sounds like you and you’re ready for your next career move, please apply through this portal or for a confidential chat or more information, get in touch with the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446.

job.title: Chief Engineer
job.description:
This newly created civil engineering leadership role will help shape the next phase of growth and optimisation for a highly regarded multidisciplinary civil construction and infrastructure company. You will lead and develop multi-site engineering and project delivery teams, strengthen risk and assurance practices, and position the Group’s technical capability for continued success as it expands into new markets.

Lattey Group is a multidisciplinary construction and engineering company with 75 years of market experience and 100 plus people across their Hastings and Levin sites. Its reputation for innovative, safe and efficient infrastructure solutions is built across five key divisions, including civil engineering, precast concrete manufacturing, crane hire, and the highly effective HEX-LOC® system.

As Chief Engineer, you will be Lattey Group’s senior engineering authority; providing engineering leadership across bridge, structural, piling, marine, foundation, precast and infrastructure construction projects delivered throughout New Zealand.

Your responsibilities will span engineering and people leadership, governance, technical assurance, and frontline civil engineering decisions across the Group’s physical works, construction methodologies and project delivery. You’ll provide independent oversight and direction across project planning, site assessment, option development, design and sign-off, constructability, construction methodology, technical risk, compliance, and delivery, including across engineered lift plans, critical lifts, crane-related engineering activities and associated construction risks.

You will also oversee site assessments and design solutions to optimise the use of their highly regarded HEX-LOC® system. This includes assessing technical suitability, defining system configurations and design boundaries, and developing robust solutions that deliver durable, resilient, sustainable, whole-of-life value for clients.

This will suit a Chartered Professional Engineer, or an experienced senior engineering leader with the ability to achieve or maintain chartered status. You must be equally confident leading people, setting engineering standards, and providing timely technical direction to frontline teams. You will combine sound judgement in managing engineering risk and opportunity with a natural, engaging leadership style. A capable team is already in place; your focus will be to build its capability further, and to represent the Group as a trusted technical authority with clients, designers, regulators, asset owners, and the wider engineering profession.

If you have the engineering expertise, an engaging approach to team leadership, and ambition to lead in a substantial civil and infrastructure business, we welcome your interest. Lattey Group has big growth plans, with the innovation, capability, and experience to expand well beyond the region. Remuneration and reward reflect the scope and seniority of this role. Please apply through this portal or, for a confidential discussion, contact Rachel Cornwall at Populous People on 0272 565 620.

job.title: Transport Dispatcher - $40 - $60/hour
job.description:
If you love the thought of keeping big wheels moving and you want to be part of a fast-moving, well-run privately owned transport business, then this is a great role for you to consider. Experience in dispatch and freight will be rewarded.
  
Our client are specialists in log transport, providing log cartage services to customers across the North Island. They are well established, have a great reputation and pride themselves on investing in quality machinery and people.
  
As their Transport Dispatcher, you will sit right in the heart of the business. You will be responsible for effectively coordinating the transportation of log loads from various locations, to ensure customer and company KPIs are met as well as ensuring maximum cartage capacity is reached for each truck. You’ll coordinate and manage the schedules of trucks ensuring pickup and delivery targets are met, maintain all logistics data via in house software, and monitor and report on daily dispatch. You’ll be good at building credibility with each of the drivers, ensuring they have all the information they need to be set up for each day. You’ll have your finger on the pulse and be ready to respond and find solutions to any interruptions or issues to the schedule. There is complexity that sits around the grading of logs, and destinations in which these can go to, so you’ll need to be able to quickly come up to speed with these standards.
  
There are lots of moving parts here and an environment where plans can change quickly, so you must be good prioritizing workloads and communicating openly and clearly with where things are at.
  
This role will be well suited to those experienced working in dispatch. Ideally you will come from a dispatch role within the logging transport industry, however we are open to considering candidates from other industries. You must be level headed, be known for your problem-solving skills and have the ability to think quick on your feet. You’ll have strong relationship skills and be able to build rapport quickly with the drivers. If you have your HT license, that will be a real bonus.
  
You must relate to the pace and customer centric focus of a privately held company where the owners are hands on and play an active part in the business. You’ll be confident navigating various software systems and driving efficiencies. You may be working in a logging, forestry or transport company currently and looking for that next challenge, or you may or you could be an experienced log truck driver looking to move into an office-based role.
  
This role will be well remunerated. If you have the required background, then please apply now through the Seek portal or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 to learn more.

job.title: Water Operations Analyst - Water Hawke's Bay
job.description:
This is a great opportunity to be part of the Water Hawke's Bay (WHB) build. You will be joining a really great team of people focussed on the success of water for Hawke’s Bay.
  
If you have three water expertise and you are keen to be part of a team making a lasting contribution in terms of how water services and infrastructure is set up and managed across the Hawke’s Bay region moving forward, then you should take a look at this Water Operations Analyst role.
  
This will be suited to those with water expertise, and keen to make sure water systems and assets are set up well for future success. Ideally you will have an engineering background; either way you’ll relate to and be able to help run a fine- tooth comb over water services assets and operations. You may already be in the region, in a council or consulting environment and want to play a part in helping with the transition of the current water services delivery models into Water Hawkes Bay. Or you may be outside of Hawkes Bay and keen to relocate here for a stunning summer in the sun while you work closely with this highly engaged transition team.
  
This is a fixed term role; running through to June 2027. It could suit a contractor or those looking for affixed term IEA. We need you to be on the ground, and in the office in Hastings, as there is a high degree of face to  face engagement and inter-entity review required here.
  
Water Hawke’s Bay is a council-controlled organisation (CCO) jointly owned by Hastings District, Napier City and Central Hawke’s Bay district councils, established under the Government’s Local Water Done Well Reforms. WHB is governed by an independent and commercially accountable Board; this is a chance to join a high performing team determined to get this right for the region. This transition team will ensure that Water Hawke’s Bay is ready to begin delivering drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater services from 1 July 2027 with a focus on providing safe and reliable water services for generations to come. In this role, you will ensure services are transferred to WHB with minimal disruption to customers and the communities. This is a fixed term role until 30 June 2027.
  
You will work within the Operational Services Workstream, analysing and then helping guide decisions that will shape the operational frameworks, processes and service delivery arrangements that will support day-to-day operations. Much of this work starts with understanding how water services are delivered today - working alongside operational teams across the three councils and other stakeholders. You will help define how those services carry across into WHB, and lead the decisions on risk, compliance and regulatory obligations that go with them. Your scope will span the transition of operational data, service delivery readiness, and operational contracts and processes. Depending on your background, you may also contribute to other technical work packages within the workstream, such as Resilience, Incident and Emergency Management, Stormwater – Operational Delivery and Health and Safety.
  
To succeed in this role, you must have an analytical and curious mindset, be great with systems and information flow, and ideally bring a technical knowledge of three waters operations. Water expertise will be highly regarded. Either way you will have the ability to translate operational knowledge into frameworks and service delivery models that work in practice. You are likely to be working in an operational, engineering or technical role within local government, a water utility or a related organisation.
  
If you have the required expertise and can build credibility and trusted relationships quickly, we would love to hear from you. Please apply through this portal. Or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.
